newsitem.title: USA: Network Computing cuts computer prices.
newsitem.headline: Network Computing cuts computer prices.

text.p: Network Computing Devices Inc said on Monday it was lowering the list price of its entire line of network computers by 25 percent to 50 percent, due to increased business and lower costs.
Effective immediately, the company said retail prices for its line of Universal Network Computers now ranged from $695 for the company's Explora entry-level model up through $2,895 for its HMXpro24.

New prices were the result of economies of scale obtained from shipments to International Business Machines Corp, increased volume from the growth of indirect sales channels and the adoption of low-discount, value-pricing for network computers, the company said.
Network Computing also said it expected its North American reseller buiness to account for 40 percent of revenues, up from 20 percent, by the end of 1997.
Through a new strategic empahsis on indirect sales partners, the company said it was expanding its sales volumes without raising operating expenses.
Network Computing also said lower costs were partly due to its relationship with IBM.
Because Network Computing manufactured the IBM Network Station, it was able to leverage volume purchases of components across both IBM's and its own products.
